findings.text: G1025's capability name and goal-schema rule contradict G1025's own design. G1027 §5 names it `release_lines`, says goal schema 2 needs no capability, and cites 'its design, lines 55 and 258'. G1025's current design (blob f240bd5, design attempt 3) names the capability `branching` (lines 19, 71-73, 322, 350) and says both a policy with settings.branching and a schema-2 goal require it. Capability names go into users' settings.engine.requires, so the two goals must agree. Fix: make it a rule that the goal adding a capability names it. Use `branching` (or 'the name G1025's design chooses'), drop or reconcile the schema-2 claim, and remove the stale line references. Also recommend G1025, which is being redesigned, take depends_on 1027 now at no cost. That removes its 'merges before G1027' branch and the last next-minor race.

The capability rule covers less than SPEC §4.5's bump list, and the docs/design edits miss where the floor is defined. §3.6's rule covers only new optional settings keys, record or finding keys and node fields. SPEC §4.5's 'What ships with an engine.min bump (one list)' also includes: a new goal schema; fingerprint, canonical-JSON, code_tree or change semantics; any op version; the lease message format; and any new POLICY or workflow key, field or op. SPEC §4.8 and DESIGN D4 tie fingerprint-version bumps to an engine.min bump, and SPEC's op-version rule (line 1565) does the same. Unless these are restated, a future FP_VERSION or op-semantics change ships with no floor. The docs list also misses SPEC blockers kinds (536), the exit table (610, engine_too_new), the tolerant read (679), the new and start verb rows (1975-1976), the REPAIR summaries (2266, 2269) and test item 75 (2365), plus DESIGN §3.10 floor and ceiling bullets (581-589), the settings list (621), the failure table (793) and invariant 21 (1262). Test 10's grep does not cover docs/design. Fix: restate the §4.5 list as 'What ships with a new capability', with every item (goal schema still gated by GOAL_SCHEMAS). Make §3.6 and the schemas.py comment match it. Change §4.8, the op-version sentence and D4 to 'together with a new capability'. List these sections in §4, and extend test 10's grep (engine.min bump|REQUIRES_MIN|engine_too_new|requires_min) to docs/design, excluding HISTORY.md.

output.summary: The core is sound and answers the owner's question. Capability names replace a shared version counter, one file per capability removes the merge race, and the plugin-version-plus-package-revision build id separates dev builds. I checked these claims against c3791a0: the floor check, policy_floor, SETTINGS_SHAPE, package_provenance (which skips pycache), the bundle's version rewrite, the legacy cache key and the REPAIR trailer greps. Both G1022 merge orders are covered, G1024 already depends on 1027, and G1027 depending on 1017 is the right shape under G1017's rule. Two findings, no owner questions. F1: G1025's capability is named release_lines here but branching in G1025's current design, which also requires it for goal schema 2. F2: the new capability rule is narrower than the list in SPEC §4.5 (fingerprint and canonical semantics, op versions, lease format, workflow keys and ops), and the docs/design edit list and stale-reference test miss several places where SPEC and DESIGN define the floor and ceiling.

spec:
The owner's question (2026-11-01): "what is engine.min? I don't see how it can work off of dev branch because we only compute semantic version on merge to main". Today the engine carries a hand-maintained ENGINE_VERSION (engine/__init__.py, 1.1.0 since G1000), POLICY has settings.engine.min, and the CLI refuses writes when engine.min > ENGINE_VERSION (store.py:457). The number is unrelated to the product's semantic-release version, and it fails in three ways: builds installed from dev report whatever __init__.py says, so one number covers different engines (CLI_USAGE already notes a pre-G1015 dev build also reports 1.0.0); goals in flight race for the next number (G1022 and G1024 both had to say "whichever merges second takes the next minor"); and the owner has to track two version numbers. The owner chose capabilities instead.

1. The engine declares a set of capability names (e.g. `lens_findings`, `lens_skips`, `policy_update`, `release_lines`), one per format or behaviour that an older engine must not touch. A goal that adds such a format adds its capability name in its own PR; no ordering between goals.
2. POLICY declares `settings.engine.requires: [names]`. The CLI refuses writes, as engine_too_old does today, when any required capability is missing, and the message names the missing ones and says to upgrade the plugin.
3. Migration: `engine.min` keeps working for repositories that have it (map 1.0.0 and 1.1.0 to their capability sets, or keep the comparison during a transition; decide in the design) and validate warns that it is deprecated. ENGINE_VERSION is removed or kept only as display, and goal commits record the capabilities (or a build id) instead of `Engine: <version>`. Legacy detection's cache key (legacy.py) stops depending on ENGINE_VERSION.
4. The goals that would raise ENGINE_VERSION (G1022, G1024, G1025, and any later one) declare capabilities instead; this goal names theirs if they merge after it, and G1000's 1.1.0 becomes the capability `lens_findings` (impact/material, filters, notes).
5. This repository: the lens policy branch (G1000 rollout step 3, after G1022) requires the capabilities its graph needs instead of raising engine.min. The owner confirmed the Codex agent on the 15b59a5 plugin is finished, so locking out 1.0 engines is approved.

Acceptance:
- Engine tests: a policy requiring a capability the engine lacks refuses writes with the names; one it has proceeds; engine.min still works per the migration rule with a deprecation warning; two goals adding different capabilities merge without conflict.
- CLI_USAGE, MIGRATING and REPAIR ("Upgrade the engine" recipe) describe requires.
- This PR edits docs/design for its contract changes and adds a HISTORY §4 row (G1017's rule).
title: Replace ENGINE_VERSION and engine.min with declared engine capabilities
